author: historian-agent:m-8
title: Temple of Heaven
summary: The Temple of Heaven in Beijing is the Ming and Qing imperial complex where emperors offered sacrifice to heaven and prayed for harvests. Its Altar of Heaven and Earth was completed with the Forbidden City in 1420; separate sacrifices to heaven were decided in 1530, and the present layout was reached by 1749. The three-tiered Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests, about 38 m tall, was rebuilt after a fire in 1889.

uncertainty.note: Start is the completion of the original Altar of Heaven and Earth in 1420 (UNESCO); the circular Hall of Prayer was built in 1545 (Temple of Heaven Park) after the 1530 decision to separate sacrifices. End is the present.

as_recorded.value: the original Altar of Heaven and Earth was completed together with the Forbidden City in 1420
In 1545 (the 24th year of the Ming-dynasty Jiajing Emperor’s reign), it was rebuilt as a triple-eave circular structure
In 1889 the Hall of Prayers for Abundant Harvests was destroyed by fire

phases.description: The rectangular Great Sacrificial Hall of 1420 was rebuilt in 1545 as a triple-eave circular hall (the ICOMOS evaluation says the large hall was dismantled fifteen years after the 1530 decision and replaced by the round Hall of Daxiang).
In 1751 all roof tiles were replaced with blue ones and the hall took its present name, Hall of Prayers for Abundant Harvests.
Destroyed by fire in 1889 and meticulously reconstructed soon afterwards with original materials and techniques; the year of completion is not given.

reviewer_note: Model is the Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests only, shape 'tower' (cylindrical hall with conical triple roof; closest allowed shape, domed_building was the alternative). Other web accounts give diameters of 30, 32 or 36 m (not opened); the two official pages opened agree on about 24 m between the outer eave columns, which is the column ring, not the marble base or eaves. The 'restored' phase starts at the fire year because the sources give no reconstruction date. Place point is the Hall (OSM way, matches UNESCO XML within 0.1 km); the whole property is 273 ha. Spotcheck cannot match the ICOMOS PDF phrases (1889 fire, fifteen years later) verbatim because its two-column layout interleaves lines; I confirmed them by reading the extracted text.
